_meta.purpose: Objective answer keys for review items. Each question is binary or single-fact and verifiable by anyone from the paper's own text, so the ground truth needs no severity judgement and no adjudication of a scientific dispute. A thorough review answers all of them; a shallow one misses some. That is the discrimination R1 cannot provide, because R1's paper is well-calibrated and its expected detection rate sits near 0.35 -- the worst place to see a change at n=5.
_meta.why_not_a_faulted_paper: R5 was first designed around a paper with an unambiguous fault. Two candidates were fetched and rejected on the same criterion, and the pattern is structural: a fault unambiguous enough that every reviewer grades it alike usually gets retracted (notorious), corrected (gone from the text), or stays contested. See items.md R5.
_meta.scoring: Per question: `correct` if the run asserts the key's answer, `incorrect` if it asserts the opposite, `unaddressed` if neither fires. Report all three -- a review that never raises a question is failing differently from one that gets it wrong.

R5.paper: Jones J, Copi CJ, Starkman GD, Akrami Y, 'Strong Evidence Against a Statistically Isotropic Universe', arXiv:2310.12859v3
R5.key_derived: 2026-08-10, by fetching https://arxiv.org/html/2310.12859v3 and reading the full text. Version-pinned: v3 was current at authoring and later versions may answer differently.

data-availability-statement.question: Does the paper carry an explicit Data Availability statement?
data-availability-statement.answer: No. It names its source in the text -- 'the data maps, masks, and best-fit theoretical LCDM power spectrum provided by the Planck 2018 data release found on the Planck Legacy Archive' -- but there is no formal statement.

analysis-code-released.question: Are the authors' own analysis codes released?
analysis-code-released.answer: No. Third-party tools are named (healpy, HEALPix, NaMaster) but no custom code is released.

blinding-or-preregistration.question: Does the paper state that the analysis was blinded or pre-registered?

trials-count-quantified.question: Does the paper state how many candidate statistics were considered before the four were selected?
trials-count-quantified.answer: No. It says 'Many statistics have been studied and many have been found to be anomalous' and acknowledges omitting others, but gives no count. This is the load-bearing gap for any trials-factor correction, and it is checkable without adjudicating whether the paper's look-elsewhere treatment is adequate.

dataset-identified.question: Which CMB data release and mask does the analysis use?
dataset-identified.answer: Planck 2018, component-separated Commander/NILC/SEVEM/SMICA maps, common mask.

systematics-separated.question: Are systematic uncertainties reported separately from statistical ones?
systematics-separated.answer: No. The analysis reports p-values from simulations; systematics are not broken out.

funding-disclosed.question: Is funding disclosed with named funders?
funding-disclosed.answer: Yes. Jump Trading Graduate Fellowship, NASA ATP grant RES240737, DOE grant DESC0009946, Spanish Research Agency / Severo Ochoa.
